basics.name: Haruki Yajima
basics.label: B.S. Student in Information and Communication Engineering
basics.summary: B.S. student at The University of Tokyo working on machine learning systems, model efficiency, and trustworthy AI.

work.name: Matsui Laboratory, The University of Tokyo
work.summary: Proposed a prediction-preserving pruning method for decision-tree ensembles.
highlights: Achieved up to around 30 percent higher compression than baseline pruning methods while preserving predictions.

work.name: MinD in a Device
work.summary: Built reproducible benchmarking infrastructure for 3D reconstruction and SLAM models.
highlights: Standardized data and evaluation pipelines across multiple scenes.
Benchmarked runtime, memory usage, and geometric accuracy against LiDAR references.
Developed reusable experiment workflows with Weights and Biases.

work.name: freee K.K.
work.summary: Contributed to IAM services for authentication and authorization.
highlights: Conducted API feasibility analysis to improve login experience.
Designed and prototyped a passkey-based authentication flow.
Submitted pull requests to improve internal design system components.

work.name: Rakuten
work.position: Web Development Intern (One-Week Summer Short Internship 2024)
work.summary: Participated in a one-week Summer Short Internship 2024 online program.
highlights: Worked with other interns to develop a web app for disaster prevention.
Mainly handled backend processing using Python.

projects.name: LabSpeak
projects.summary: Dockerized full-stack application (Next.js, FastAPI, Postgres) for research-lab conversation practice.
highlights: Integrated LLM-based dialogue generation with streaming responses via Server-Sent Events.
Implemented real-time STT and TTS interaction for voice-based practice.
Designed a provider-agnostic interface for OpenAI-compatible APIs.

projects.name: PrompDojo (Gemini 3 Tokyo Hackathon)
projects.summary: Real-time multiplayer prompt quiz powered by Gemini.
highlights: Awarded 3rd place out of 70 teams at Gemini 3 Tokyo Hackathon.
Built with Next.js, TypeScript, Firebase, and Gemini API.
Implemented realtime room flow, round progression, and scoring UX.
